cells.tense: The read on the room arrives first, and the pick follows after it.
cells.act: write the order things go in
cells.ask: Lay out the sequence you want the next month to run in — order only, on a page kept where calls get made. Glance at it before the next choice; the page holds the shape while the day shifts around it.
cells.core:
The read on a room shows up before anyone explains it, and you don't bother arguing with it. That's why direction comes easier to you than it looks from outside — the answer tends to be there already, and the pick is mostly agreeing to it. When a call is right, it's settled before any reason assembles, and you've quit waiting for the reason to arrive first.

What you can add now is a frame around the picks. Put the sequence somewhere you'll look, so direction holds on the tired days and the talked-at days. A written order isn't doubt in your read; it's the shelf the read sits on. Keep it short enough to take in at a glance, and let what you sense keep revising it.
cells.sheetLine: You sense the call before you can explain it.
cells.verb: Knowing what matters before the reason shows

cells.tense: More will be gathered, because the pile still looks too thin to pick from.
cells.act: choose the light to steer by and turn toward it
cells.ask: Hold one line to yourself about what this effort is actually for, then aim the next move at that rather than at another fact to collect — privately, before you act.
cells.core:
You're collecting. More facts, more opinions, one more look before committing, and the pile has grown wide enough to shelter behind. It reads as care; from outside it reads as a wall. Underneath it the thing you actually want is still sitting there, and it hasn't been faced directly in some time. Your read on it is fine. It's the gathering around the read that does the stalling.

Pick a light and steer. Not certainty — a direction you'd be sorry to lose, held plainly to yourself, and the next move aimed there. You still won't have all of it. You'll be moving, which beats being sure.
cells.sheetLine: You keep collecting so the choice can stay unmade.
cells.verb: Knowing what matters before the reason shows

cells.tense: The call already sits behind you, and you stand at the door regardless.
cells.act: sketch the whole of it badly, on one page, and keep the sketch
cells.ask: Give an hour to a rough sketch of where this could land next year, working only from what you've already been through. Imperfect is fine. Fold it away somewhere you'll find it again.
cells.core:
Your own read carries less weight than it used to, so it gets checked against whoever is nearby, and their version outlasts yours. A call already sits behind you — taking it may have happened without your notice, and nothing has moved in that direction since. The confusion has filled the whole space, and it is harder to stand in than any wrong answer would be.

Let it stay unclear and work from what you've been through. Not the whole of it — a rough sketch of where this could land, built only from what you've lived, and kept. Not knowing isn't a gate you pass before walking. It's the ground under your feet right now.
cells.sheetLine: You ask around for an answer you've already given.
cells.verb: Knowing what matters before the reason shows

cells.tense: A read is steering the pick while you tell it as a coin toss.
cells.act: let an exchange flow both ways
cells.ask: Take what's offered without talking it down, and pass along what's wanted without keeping score. One exchange each way, noticed, then stop counting entirely.
cells.core:
Some of the calls you've filed as spontaneous were settled earlier — by a read that arrived before you sat down — and the story you tell about it is a coin toss that happened to land well. It works, which is why it goes unremarked. The plainest form of this sense is how quickly you can tell a fair trade from a rigged one, and you can, right up until you're asked to say who did the telling.

Let something move both directions. What's offered, taken; what's wanted, given; no running tally on either side. That's the earlier form of the same sense, and doing it is how the sense surfaces where you can see it. Nothing to announce. Just the exchange, moving both ways.
cells.sheetLine: You decide by feel, then call it chance.
cells.verb: Knowing what matters before the reason shows

attempts.check: The draft risks claiming the person already knows things and just won't consult it — the record only supports that knowing happens and lands unargued, not that they possess it as a felt fact, and Too Little especially may not recognise any knowing at all right now. The reader could reasonably say they are simply confused, not 'disowning' anything, so the Too Little cell locates them at the door without saying what put them there. The ask survives being wrong: if the read is off, keeping the dream picture and a settled order still costs nothing and teaches what the person actually reaches for. The sentence that serves me over them is 'You already knew' in any form — cut, because it tells them their own life back and anoints the method instead of offering one.
